output.summary: An evergreen flowering plant of unknown original range, ti is believed native from Bangladesh through Southeast Asia, southern China and Taiwan to New Guinea and northern Australia. Its palm-like form carries fan-like clusters of green, red or variegated leaves. Roots and young leaves can be cooked as survival food, while Polynesian green forms supply processed sweet rhizomes and Hawaiian roots can be fermented and distilled.
output.edibilityNote: Roots and young leaves are cooked as survival food; Polynesian green forms yield processed sweet rhizomes, and Hawaiian fermented roots are distilled into alcohol.
